facts.statement: The genus Invictibellatrix contains only one species, I. amberina, which is known from a single braincase fossil.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Invictibellatrix amberina, known from a single braincase.

facts.statement: The fossil material of Invictibellatrix was discovered in the Wessex Formation on the Isle of Wight, United Kingdom.
facts.quote: The Invictibellatrix fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the Wessex Formation on the Isle of Wight, United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was sold to the Natural History Museum in London in May 1924 by the widow of collector Reginald Walter Hooley.
facts.quote: It was sold to the museum in May 1924 by the widow of the collector Reginald Walter Hooley.

facts.statement: Cassius Morrison and colleagues formally described Invictibellatrix amberina as a new genus and species in 2026, designating specimen NHMUK PV R 6775 as the holotype.
facts.quote: In 2026, Cassius Morrison and colleagues described Invictibellatrix amberina as a new genus and species of megaraptoran theropod based on these fossil remains, designating NHMUK PV R 6775 as the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Invictibellatrix is estimated to have had a body mass of 200 to 300 kg and a body length of approximately 4 meters.
facts.quote: Invictibellatrix is estimated to have a body mass between 200–300 kg and a body length of around 4 m.

facts.statement: The crest on the back of the Invictibellatrix skull is lightly transversely compressed with an hourglass profile.
facts.quote: The crest on the back of the skull is lightly tranvsersely compressed and has an hourglass profile.

facts.statement: The genus Invictibellatrix was established by Morrison et al. in 2026.
Invictibellatrix is classified within the parent group Megaraptora.
Invictibellatrix lived during the Barremian stage, between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Invictibellatrix lived in the Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, UK, during the Barremian age of the Lower Cretaceous.
The discovery of Invictibellatrix adds to the known diversity of Early Cretaceous European coelurosaurs, which now includes tyrannosauroids, maniraptoriforms, and megaraptorans.

rejected.statement: Invictibellatrix is an extinct genus of megaraptoran theropod dinosaur whose name means "unconquered warrior".
rejected.quote: Invictibellatrix (Latin: "unconquered warrior") is an extinct genus of megaraptoran theropod dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian age) Wessex Formation of England.

rejected.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests that Invictibellatrix is distantly related to all previously named theropods found in the same stratigraphic unit.
rejected.quote: Phylogenetic analysis and comparative anatomy indicate that Invictibellatrix is distantly related to all previously named theropods from this stratigraphic unit.
